name: Mercer Museum
customer: Tool people, history fans, architecture students
unique: A concrete castle built to hold one man's collection of pre-industrial American tools, with a whaleboat hanging from the ceiling and a walkway that spirals up through six floors.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and people describe it as a cathedral of hand tools; allow two hours because every case has something strange.

name: Fonthill Castle
unique: Henry Mercer's concrete house with 44 rooms, 32 stairwells and a ceiling of Moravian tiles, built by hand with no architect and no plan.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and the stairs are steep; visitors say it feels like a medieval house built by a obsessive.

name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
unique: The winter camp where Washington's army survived 1777 with a reconstructed log city, earthworks you can walk and a 3,500 acre park with a bike trail through it.
buzz: The ranger talks and the Muhlenberg Brigade huts are the best part; the loop road is flat and the park is free, which surprises people.

name: Bryn Athyn Cathedral
company: General Church of the New Jerusalem
customer: Architecture people, stained glass fans, quiet seekers
unique: A Gothic cathedral built by hand in the 1910s by craftsmen who worked without straight lines, with glass made on the grounds and a hilltop view over the Pennypack valley.
buzz: Architects call the craftsmanship a century ahead of its time; the cathedral is free and the neighboring Glencairn Museum is the paid tour.

name: Brandywine River Museum
unique: A converted gristmill on the Brandywine holding three generations of Wyeth paintings, including the Olson House canvases and N.C. Wyeth's illustrations.
buzz: The top floor galleries with the Andrew Wyeth rooms are the reason to come; the mill windows look out on the river he painted.

name: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
unique: The ridge where the modern raptor count began, with a lookout over the Kittatinny where hundreds of hawks and eagles pass on a good September day.
buzz: Volunteers with clickers will teach you to identify a bird on the wing; the North Lookout is a short steep walk and the trail system continues for miles.

name: Reading Pagoda
unique: A seven story Japanese pagoda built on a Pennsylvania mountain in 1908 by a manufacturer who never saw Japan, now a landmark above the city with a view of five counties.
buzz: It is a free oddity with a real view; the tower interior is closed most of the time and the hillside garden is where people sit.

name: Yuengling Brewery Tour
unique: America's oldest brewery, dug into a hillside where the cellars are 150 feet of hand cut sandstone and the tour ends with samples in a 19th century bottling house.
buzz: The cave cellars are the part people remember; tours are free but fill early and the tasting is short.

name: Pioneer Tunnel Coal Mine
unique: A narrow gauge mine train that carries you 1,800 feet into a working anthracite vein, then a steam locomotive ride on the surface along the old colliery.
buzz: The guides are former miners and the mine is cold; children like the train and adults like the stories about breaker boys.

name: Knoebels Amusement Resort
unique: A free admission park in the woods with three wood coasters, a 1913 carousel, a coal fired steam train and pierogies, all priced by the ride.
buzz: Enthusiasts rank Phoenix among the best wooden coasters in the world; families like that parking and admission are free and food is cheap.

name: Bloomsburg Fair
unique: The largest agricultural fair in the state, nine days of draft horse pulls, a mile of food stands and a grandstand concert series in a town of 15,000.
buzz: Locals take the week off; the livestock barns and the harness racing are the real fair and the midway is the noise around it.

name: Horseshoe Curve
unique: A 1.8 mile curve engineered in 1854 to lift the Pennsylvania Railroad over the Alleghenies, with a funicular up to a viewing park where 100 car freight trains still grind past.
buzz: Check the train schedule at the visitor center and time your visit; the funicular and the view of the curve from above are the whole experience.

name: Railroaders Memorial Museum
customer: Train people, families, labor history fans
unique: The old PRR master mechanics building holding a K4 steam locomotive, a cab you can climb into and the story of the Altoona shops that built and repaired the railroad.
buzz: The simulator and the cab are for children and the labor history galleries are for adults; combine it with Horseshoe Curve on one ticket.

name: Johnstown Flood Museum
unique: The 1889 flood that killed 2,200 people when a private dam gave way, told in the old Carnegie library with a relief map, survivor accounts and an Oscar winning film.
buzz: The film runs on a loop and still lands; visitors say the scale of the disaster is hard to hold until you see the map of the valley.

name: Johnstown Inclined Plane
unique: The steepest vehicular inclined plane in the world at 70 percent grade, built as an escape route after the flood and still carrying cars and people up the hill.
buzz: The ride is short and the view from the top over the Conemaugh valley is the point; the operator will explain the counterweight.

name: Flight 93 National Memorial
unique: A field in Somerset County where the fourth hijacked plane came down, marked by a white marble wall that follows the flight path and a tower of wind chimes with a bell for each passenger.
buzz: The walk from the visitor center to the wall is a quarter mile and the sound of the wind chimes is what people describe; it is quiet and free.

name: Laurel Hill State Park
unique: A CCC built lake and beach in the Laurel Highlands with a hemlock gorge trail and a spillway that freezes into ice climbs in winter.
buzz: The beach is the summer draw and the gorge trail is the walk; the ice climbing at the spillway is a local winter secret.

name: Penn's Cave
unique: The only all water cave tour in the country, a flat bottom boat through a limestone passage under a mountain and out the other side, with a wildlife park above.
buzz: The boat is the whole tour and children love it; the cave is 52 degrees and the wildlife park is a separate walk.

name: Berkey Creamery
unique: The university dairy that makes ice cream from its own herd and sells it in a plant on campus, with a viewing window over the production floor.
buzz: The lines run out the door on football weekends and the Peachy Paterno was renamed; the half gallon is the move if you are driving.

name: Little League World Series
unique: The world championship for 12 year olds, played on a hillside field where fans sit on the grass and teams from Japan, Venezuela and Texas stay in the same village.
buzz: Admission is free and the hill fills early; locals say the international teams and the Lamade Stadium atmosphere beat most professional games.

name: Millionaires' Row
unique: A street of lumber baron mansions from the 1880s and 1890s, some 40 rooms with ballrooms and Tiffany windows, when Williamsport was the lumber capital of the world.
buzz: The self guided walking tour brochure is at the visitor center; several houses are now law offices and one is a museum.

name: Pennsylvania Grand Canyon
unique: A 47 mile gorge of Pine Creek with two rim overlooks, a rail trail at the bottom and 800 foot rock walls that turn orange in October.
buzz: The west rim overlooks are the easy view and the Turkey Path is the steep way down; the canyon is at its best in the first week of October.

name: Pine Creek Rail Trail
unique: A 62 mile crushed stone trail down the floor of the Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania along Pine Creek, with shuttle services that drop you at the top.
buzz: The down hill run from Ansonia to Jersey Shore is the standard half day; the shuttle books out in fall and the trail is flat enough for hybrids.

name: Kinzua Bridge Skywalk
unique: A 301 foot tall railroad viaduct that a tornado tore down in 2003, now a glass floored observation deck at the edge of the wreckage with the twisted towers still standing in the valley.
buzz: The glass floor is the thrill and the fallen towers are the photo; the walk out is 600 feet and the valley is best in fall.

name: Eldred World War II Museum
unique: A volunteer museum in a small town with a room for each theater of the war, mannequins in original uniforms and a collection of home front ration books and letters.
buzz: Visitors say the personal donations make it better than the big museums; it is free will donation and the volunteers are often veterans.

name: Zippo/Case Museum
unique: The factory museum where the lighter that became a soldier's talisman is displayed with the case knives, including the prototypes and the lifetime guarantee repair bench.
buzz: Collectors come from overseas and the staff still repair any Zippo for free; the museum is free and takes an hour.

name: French Azilum
unique: A planned refuge for French aristocrats fleeing the revolution, built in the Pennsylvania wilderness in 1793, with the foundation of the house meant for Marie Antoinette.
buzz: The story is better than the remains and the volunteer guides tell it well; it is a quiet stop on a back road along the Susquehanna.

name: Polymath Park
unique: A hillside with three Frank Lloyd Wright houses, two of them moved here from elsewhere, that you can tour and then sleep in.
buzz: Wright people call it the only place to stay overnight in a Wright house in the east; tours need booking and the houses are small.

name: Idlewild Park
unique: A 1878 trolley park in the Laurel Highlands with Storybook Forest, a 1930s walk through nursery rhymes, and a wooden coaster in the woods.
buzz: Parents say Storybook Forest is the reason to come before children turn eight; the water park and the coaster extend the day.

name: Hersheypark
unique: A chocolate company's employee picnic ground turned 121 acre park with 15 coasters, a water park and a zoo, ringed by the smell of cocoa from the factory.
buzz: Candymonium and Skyrush are the coaster draws; buy tickets online, arrive at opening and use the preview night if you are staying over.

name: Hershey's Chocolate World
unique: A free visitor center with a singing animatronic ride through the chocolate making process, a factory viewing line and a create your own chocolate bar counter.
buzz: The ride is free and dated in a way people love; the lines for the custom bar are long and the parking is paid.
